contracts.title: IA2457 Child Exploitation and Missing Children Service
contracts.description:
Staffordshire County Council, Stoke on Trent City Council and the Staffordshire Commissioner for Police, Fire and Rescue and Crime wish to jointly commission a Child Exploitation and Missing Children Service.  
      
The Service will directly contribute to the three strategic outcomes of our Pan-Staffordshire Child Exploitation Strategy:
      • Children and young people are not victims of Child Exploitation.
      • Children and young people are protected from Child Exploitation by parents/ carers, communities, professionals and businesses.
      • Children, young people and adults are not perpetrators and/or groomed to facilitate Child Exploitation.
      
The Service will also be responsible for the delivery of the Return Home Interview (RHI) process across the County and City in line with The Department for Education's, 2014 Statutory guidance on children who run away or go missing from home or care.
      
The provision will offer a flexible approach to meeting the needs of children between 0-17 years and young adults with special educational needs and disabilities beyond their 18th birthday if they have an education health and care plan.  The provision will also offer a flexible approach to care leavers beyond their 18th birthday. 
      
The Provider will offer the Service, and/or refer to other agencies where appropriate.  The Service must be provided and accessible in each of the eight (8) districts/ boroughs in Staffordshire and in the city of Stoke-on-Trent.  
      
The current contracts, which are in place for the delivery of some of these Services come to an end on 31st August 2022.

Interested suppliers should register on the Proactis e-tendering system: https://supplierlive.proactisp2p.com/Account/Login and then register an interest in this opportunity.

contracts.description:

Staffordshire County Council is committed to working alongside Providers of all Community-Based Opportunities for Older People & Physical Disability and the VCSE sector to support and empower our communities. The Council therefore wish to meet with Providers to informally talk about:
•	current Day Care Services and Community-Based Opportunities in each district locality
•	scoping need and gaps in service provision in each district locality
•	identifying what aspirations you have for future service delivery. 

The main purpose of this Market Engagement is to consider how Day Care Services and Community-Based Opportunities for Older People & Physical Disability across Staffordshire can continue to be best provided in terms of :-
•	geographical breakdown, to ensure appropriate service coverage 
•	improved choice of Services on offer and accessibility to Individuals.

This is a great opportunity for the Council, Providers and VCSE to work together to look at how we can:-
•	Build capacity in communities to support future service   delivery and shape the vision for the future service
• Improve and maintain individuals' health and well-being through increased independence, choice, control, dignity and quality of life. 
•	Promote independence and enable individuals to become an active member of society and the community.

Staffordshire County Council would like to hear from service providers who are interested and capable of delivering a high quality and outcome focussed Mental Health and Therapeutic Support Service for children and young people who are engaged with and/or under the supervision of the Staffordshire Youth Offending Service. 

The objectives of the Service are to improve the emotional and mental well being of children and young people who are involved in the Youth Justice System or at risk of entering the Criminal Justice System as a consequence of antisocial behaviour or coming to the attention of the Police in local communities. This will include working with families to strengthen relationships and prevent further offending behaviour. It is envisaged that Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) will be employed as a primary method for working with young people to assist them and their families to understand their behaviour and to work towards having an offence free future. 

The successful provider will be expected to develop and maintain good and effective working relationships with a range of providers to deliver an integrated service that promotes a whole system approach. This includes providing training and consultation to enhance and improve Staffordshire Youth Offending Service practitioner competence and confidence to work effectively with children and young people and their families through planned interventions relating to emotional and mental health.

contracts.title: Children & Young People's Advocacy Services
contracts.description:
Staffordshire County Council wishes to invite tenders for the provision of Children & Young People's Advocacy Services across the County of Staffordshire and the City of Stoke-on-Trent. 

The main purpose of advocacy is to encourage empowerment in order that a child or young person can make choices, assert their rights as they see them, and receive the type of services that suit their needs.

The Service Specification and outcomes have been developed around the Strategic Priorities of both Councils and delivering service user outcomes.

The overall value of the Contract is £186,700 per annum.

The Contract with the provider is expected to be initially for 2 years (1st October 2015 to 30th September 2017) and may have the options to extend by two further periods of 12 months each. First extension period would 1st October 2017 to 30th September 2018 and second extension period would be 1st October 2018 to 30th September 2019.   

The specification will include advocacy services for:
•	Looked After Children
•	Children with emotional wellbeing/mental health issues (Staffordshire only)
•	Children Subject to a Child Protection Plan 
•	Children & young people with Learning Disabilities
•	Children & young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)

The provider must be in a position to deliver advocacy services to all children and young people in these specific groups (which may, on occasion, include children and young people living/placed outside the Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent boundaries).

The service will be available to children and young people from the above groups between the ages of 5 – 18 years, and up to the age of 25 for those with SEND.

The service will also deliver a small additional element of an Independent Visitor programme for children and young people in Stoke-on-Trent only.

contracts.title: Voluntary, Community and Social enterprise (VCSE) Infrastructure and Volunteering Support Services
contracts.description:
Staffordshire County Council is looking to re-commission its support for the voluntary sector in Staffordshire, with the new contract expected to commence from May 2016. We want to support the sector to adapt to a changing public sector environment, help build capacity in the sector, develop volunteering across the county and support VCSE organisations to grow. 

Since 2013, a Provider has been commissioned to provide infrastructure and volunteering support across Staffordshire. Infrastructure support involves strategic engagement and representation for local voluntary sector groups and organisations, as well as one-to-one development and support for issues such as business planning and fundraising etc. Volunteering support involves providing organisations with advice and guidance as well as helping to match volunteers with local opportunities, and in addition supporting voluntary organisations to become ‘volunteer ready’ by providing support with recruiting and managing volunteers.

Another Provider has also been commissioned to offer specialist support to voluntary sector organisations with a focus on youth provision.  This support enables groups both to start up and become safe, strong and sustainable in the longer term, using a self assessment quality assurance process (Outcomes Dial) that targets support to where it is needed most. These support services include access to accommodation and small grants, free or low cost training, promotion and representation, networking and up to date information, advice and guidance on a range of relevant issues.

Over the coming weeks and months we will be talking to our partners in the public and private sector about how best to commission this support moving forward.
